body.heading: Waiting time is hiding everywhere
paragraphs: Kettles, microwaves, loading screens, buses that are two minutes away: a day contains dozens of small waits. Most of them are spent staring at a phone, but they could be spent moving a little.
Linking a stretch to the kettle is an old habit-design trick: attach the new behaviour to something that already happens several times a day, and it needs almost no willpower.

body.heading: Keep it gentle and simple
paragraphs: Roll your shoulders, reach slowly toward the ceiling, turn your head side to side, rise onto your toes and lower down. Move within what feels comfortable, breathe normally, and never force a position.
If you have any injury or condition, follow the advice you have been given for it, and skip anything that hurts. Gentle and regular is the whole idea; this is a stretch, not a test.

takeaway: Trade a few waiting minutes for gentle movement, several times a day.
